analysis_refs.heading: Viewing the boards
analysis_refs.text:
**All records are samples.** Project Gutenberg IDs, titles and the Gutenberg
rights wording are real. Every paper, author, journal, DOI (the `10.5555` test
prefix), arXiv ID and children's story is invented. Never copy board records
into fixtures as if they were real catalog data.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: Connected next: Book Dash
analysis_refs.text:
The public WordPress book type exposes source-native edition IDs and an explicit
language taxonomy. The catalog reported 1,116 language-edition entries and its
English taxonomy reported 214 when checked. A bounded **30-English-edition**
subset is now bundled and searchable alongside Gutenberg, textbooks and the
reviewed StoryWeaver set. This does not claim complete source coverage.

analysis_refs.heading: Connected next: Book Dash
analysis_refs.text:
The [official catalog](https://bookdash.org/books/) and
[reuse policy](https://bookdash.org/re-using-the-book-dash-content/) state that
Book Dash books are free and published under CC BY 4.0. Original creator roles
are preserved: writer, illustrator, designer, editor and any supplied translator
or photographer. The source supplies no publisher reading level for this
subset; none is inferred. These books participate in ordinary Free to read
searches; the separate EN/HI/TA pilot remains explicitly a reviewed starter set.

analysis_refs.heading: Connected next: Book Dash
analysis_refs.text:
The daily reviewed catalog workflow includes Book Dash. Positive access evidence
expires after 24 hours; failed refresh never renews stale claims. Catalog search
requires no Redis. The first scheduled run follows default-branch merge and
remains a release check.

analysis_refs.heading: Recommendation: batch the research, limit active engineering, release often
analysis_refs.text: | Fixed number of sources every day | Creates a regular research habit | An easy catalog and a complex land-record service take very different effort; pressure to hit a count can reward superficial checks | Use research-session ranges and time budgets, never a daily activation quota |

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Choose the next batch by useful coverage and shared implementation
analysis_refs.text:
Apply the master plan's mandatory gates first, then its priority weights. Compare
incremental content/language/local coverage, query/access quality, maintenance
burden and implementation effort. A large catalog consisting mostly of already
available records can be less useful than a small regional-language collection.

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Choose the next batch by useful coverage and shared implementation
analysis_refs.text:
- **Book/catalog theme:** an official reusable book export and additional origins
  demonstrably covered by it. Reuse the current book search/detail/shelf flow.
- **Industry guidance theme:** agricultural extension or construction/manufacturing
  training catalogs that share document/learning-resource mappings and useful
  task metadata. Implement cross-cutting tags with evidence for each assignment.
- **Public-document theme:** government reports, acts or civic records with a
  supported document API/export and explicit jurisdiction/version handling.
- **Geospatial theme:** one supported catalog/native query pattern, first a US
  case and an India case when both qualify; distinguish map discovery from
  feature/parcel lookup rather than pretending all services offer both.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Suggested opening sequence
analysis_refs.text:
Refresh is part of each source's delivery. Establish independent import validation
and failure reporting where needed so one source's review failure does not erase
valid results elsewhere. Never advance observation timestamps to make an expired
source appear fresh. If the existing refresh policy is too costly for a proposed
catalog, resolve that operational question before enabling it.

analysis_refs.heading: 6. Stories to expand when they are reached
analysis_refs.text:
Every selected source story names: user query/use case, expected native item,
content/industry/jurisdiction scope, connector dependency, free-access class,
source-specific acceptance, operating cost and owner. Track **qualified** and
**enabled** separately; a code merge alone does not establish either current
availability or complete catalog coverage.

analysis_refs.heading: 1. Goal and counting rules
analysis_refs.text: | Candidate origin | An identified publisher, repository, institution or community with a distinct maintained content catalog; eligibility is unproven. |

analysis_refs.heading: 1. Goal and counting rules
analysis_refs.text: | Qualified origin | A candidate whose relevant catalog or explicitly bounded subset passes the queryability, access, permissions and cost gates below. Record the tested scope and date. |

analysis_refs.heading: 1. Goal and counting rules
analysis_refs.text:
Count an origin once globally, and at most once in each relevant category.
Mirrors, language views, formats, feed endpoints, journal titles under one
publisher, and collections under one catalog do not inflate the origin count.
Separately maintained institutional catalogs can qualify independently when their
ownership, identifiers, searchable scope and evidence are recorded. An individual
article, course, podcast episode or PDF is an item, never a source.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C05 Audiobooks and recorded books | Public-domain audio publishers, LibriVox-related collections, library audio collections and publisher feeds | Regional-language volunteer reading projects, public cultural institutions and eligible accessible-book initiatives | Search API, reusable catalog or complete feeds; distinguish complete recordings, samples, abridgements and eligibility restrictions |

analysis_refs.text: | C08 Government, policy and development reports | UN/multilateral publication catalogs, national agencies, policy institutes and open repository directories | Union/state ministries, RBI, NITI Aayog, research councils and state planning bodies | Publication API/export or permitted bounded catalog; jurisdiction, report date/version and actual document access |

analysis_refs.text: | C09 School lessons, curricula and examination resources | Education ministry portals, teacher OER networks and curriculum repositories | DIKSHA organizations, SCERTs, state boards and official examination bodies | Supported catalog/search or export; board, medium, grade and curriculum year; avoid unauthorized commercial exam copies |

analysis_refs.heading: Dedicated civic-record and maps coverage columns
analysis_refs.text:
For P04, distinguish assessed ownership, registered deeds, land-rights records
and legal title; a match must retain the issuing authority's meaning. For P06/P07,
map-viewing capability and queryable geographic features are separate capabilities.
Capture geospatial fields and current/historical scope rather than presenting an
old or generalized map as a precise current property boundary. Research uses
catalog/schema examples; it does not require collecting personal ownership data.

analysis_refs.heading: 6. Queryability and free-access admission gates
analysis_refs.text: | Maintainable coverage | Defined subset/full-catalog scope, paging or bounded import behavior, refresh/deletion plan and an accountable maintainer. A handpicked record does not establish whole-catalog search. |

analysis_refs.heading: 6. Queryability and free-access admission gates
analysis_refs.text:
1. **Documented live search API**, with record resolution and bounded calls.
2. **Verified aggregator coverage**, with attributable item-level origin/host
   evidence. Confirm known items and missing/lagging coverage per origin; do not
   claim a source's complete catalog simply because it appears in an index.
3. **Official reusable metadata export/feed**, compiled into a bounded local
   search artifact. This is the existing book-catalog approach; it need not add a
   hosted service. Large imports require measured build/memory/refresh costs.
4. **Explicitly permitted structured harvesting**, only where refresh and item
   discovery are sustainable. Document the supported route and its limitations;
   a fragile browser scraper is not the default way to reach 100 sources.

analysis_refs.heading: 7. Qualification tests and evidence
analysis_refs.text:
- Five known items: exact title/ID, author where supported, at least one
  non-English/native-script item when the source claims that coverage. Check
  round-trip search → native record → actual full-item destination.
- Five topic queries chosen before inspecting results. Review top-five results
  for subject match, useful item type and accessible destination. Record
  title/subject/full-text matching limitations. Do not repeat the earlier
  Mathematics problem by accepting unrelated metadata as relevance evidence.
- For public-record/geospatial sources, substitute five appropriate record/spatial
  queries for unsupported keyword searches: jurisdiction + document number,
  address/parcel, map-sheet name, bounding box, or variable + geography + period.
  Test CRS/axis ordering, geographic boundaries, pagination/truncation and survey
  versus publication/effective dates. A documented map viewer alone does not
  establish feature queries, and an API error must never imply no ownership record.
- For industry material, test role/task relevance, applicable country/standard,
  revision date and evidence for each assigned industry tag. A shared regulator
  catalog is one origin even when it spans all twenty industries.
- Negative/gibberish queries, changed filters, punctuation and Unicode. Confirm
  empty results versus source failure. Check a second page or declare the fixed
  import scope; retain duplicates/versions correctly.
- A representative restricted/embargoed/preview item if the catalog contains
  them. Verify exclusion or clear labeling rather than inheriting a blanket
  "free source" assumption. Free-login tests distinguish an advertised offer
  from actually verified post-login access; unavailable proof is a recorded gap.
- Latency, payload size, documented quotas and bounded errors. Test throttling
  and outages with fixtures; do not overload a real service to generate a 429.
- Two independent sessions for shortlisted sources, on different days where
  practical, to detect transient success. Capture timestamp, region, request
  shape, native IDs, policy URLs and a small permitted evidence sample; no keys,
  private cookies or copied full books in evidence.

analysis_refs.heading: 7. Qualification tests and evidence
analysis_refs.text:
Suggested pilot acceptance targets, to calibrate before production: all five
known eligible items are found in the declared searchable scope; at least four
of the first five results are relevant on four of five topic queries; no known
restricted item is labeled freely readable. A specialist source can declare
exact-title-only or structured-record/spatial capability, but must not be routed
unsupported queries or counted as general topic-search coverage. A native public
catalog that searches by parcel or document ID can qualify for that declared use.
Identifier redirect services such as DOI resolvers remain supporting services;
they do not themselves establish a searchable content catalog. Small tests establish the declared sample,
not measured recall of the entire catalog. Track these capabilities separately.

analysis_refs.heading: 8. Scale the integrations without scaling infrastructure prematurely
analysis_refs.text:
Keep the research register as reviewed JSON/CSV and Markdown in Git. It is a
source catalog and evidence index, not a new hosted database. Version snapshots
and run bounded local/repository checks within the existing free allowances.

analysis_refs.heading: 8. Scale the integrations without scaling infrastructure prematurely
analysis_refs.text:
Build shared connector families only when multiple qualified candidates justify
them: native/aggregator JSON search, OAI-PMH imports, CSV/JSON/MARC exports, OPDS,
MediaWiki, repository APIs and later dataset/media/geospatial interfaces. Evaluate
documented OGC/ArcGIS services with explicit catalog, map-view and feature-query
capabilities; do not assume every deployment supports the same operations. Reuse transport and
tests while retaining per-source mappings, policies and access rules. DSpace,
EPrints or OJS software alone is not proof that a site's interface is enabled.

analysis_refs.heading: 8. Scale the integrations without scaling infrastructure prematurely
analysis_refs.text:
Future routing should be deterministic first. Show which connector/origins were
searched, bounded catalog coverage, exclusions and failures. An explicit choice
must not silently search something else. Search more sources on reader request;
any later small parallel-search design needs its own latency, cost and pagination
proof. No paid LLM routing, vector database or blanket fan-out is prerequisite.

analysis_refs.heading: 10. Progress report and immediate next batch
analysis_refs.text:
The content categories are accepted. The next research cycle uses M1 across all
20 categories and 20 industry tags with the six playbooks. In M2,
prioritize book/education/India opportunities plus US/India public records/maps
and practical industry documentation: DOAB/OAPEN publisher coverage,
national/regional literature catalogs, school textbook bodies, children's
publishers, thesis repositories, audiobook catalogs, official civic/property
catalogs, geological data and agriculture/construction/manufacturing/logistics
guidance. Recheck existing source
freshness first; new names do not solve an expired catalog or a three-item pilot.

analysis_refs.heading: Current free live profile — 2026-11-03
analysis_refs.text:
No new datastore or account resource is provisioned. The older shared profile
below is historical and no longer blocks the current paper release. Catalog
refresh/access evidence requirements remain in force.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
Shared sessions retain each source's cursor and excess records. Browser cursors
contain only a signed query/context/policy binding and shared page reference,
expire after 15 minutes, and replay without repeating provider requests. Versions
and translations retain source-native keys. Exact source-key repeats are removed;
cross-index DOI matches remain distinct until a source proves version equivalence.
Live offset indexes can change between requests; no frozen global catalog or
global result total is promised. Source observations and query coverage stay visible.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
Refresh bundled catalogs before the 24-hour positive-evidence expiry. Commands
and provenance are in [the snapshot notes](../../../server/data/content/README.md).
Offline reimports retain original observation times. Check removals, schema,
shrink protection, source permissions, host-link samples, bundle inclusion and
regressions before enabling a refreshed catalog. Never manually advance timestamps.

analysis_refs.heading: Reviewed daily refresh
analysis_refs.text:
`python tools/content/refresh_catalogs.py --output-dir /tmp/new-free-candidates`
prepares the three catalog imports in a new directory, preserving the active baseline. Any
source failure, empty/schema-invalid candidate or shrink failure leaves no
published candidate. `node tools/content/audit_snapshots.mjs /tmp/new-free-candidates`
verifies actual source identities, indexing and current reading evidence. Inspect
the report's additions, missing keys and semantic changes before updating files.
Observation-time changes are reported separately from bibliographic changes.

analysis_refs.heading: Reviewed daily refresh
analysis_refs.text:
Source sampling found Gutenberg's supplied virtual HTML route returning 404
for both HEAD and GET response headers, while the supplied direct `/files/`
HTML URL returned 200. Mapping v2 excludes virtual HTML links, chooses supplied
direct HTML where available and otherwise uses the catalog landing page. Valid
supplied EPUB/Kindle routes remain available; no file path is guessed. Download
buttons use the primary location's formats/rights, one per MIME. Other reading
locations show their own version/licence instead of inheriting the primary one.

analysis_refs.heading: Reproduced behavior
analysis_refs.text:
The revised first 20 results all contain Mathematics in their titles. This is a
metadata relevance improvement, not a claim about the best textbook for a
reader's level or a larger catalog. Genuine subject-only matches remain available
after closer matches and show `Subject: …` using the source's own metadata.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.
  Their metadata is isolated in `client/e2e/free-content-ui-fixture.js`.
- The [actual-source app flows](evidence/2026-11-01/ui-review/actual-source-flow/expanded-sources-app-flow.json)
  separately exercise the real Tamil StoryWeaver record and Book Dash edition:
  search → detail → supplied source URL → save → reload → reopen, on desktop and
  phone, including 320px/200% text. Their credits and free-account condition are
  preserved. No source account was created and post-login reading is untested.
- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.
  Only source-supplied versions/downloads/relations render; no v1/v2 list, recording,
  translation, cover art or licence is inferred to imitate sample data.
- The shared four-tab shell, desktop navigation rail and browser safe-area
  handling remain the existing app. The source sheet keeps its shared Close
  control. Catalog-subset disclosure and the owner-approved free-account group
  add necessary content beyond the original sample boards.
- Recent query history is bounded and lost on reload. It is not written to
  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.
- A fresh Europe PMC request on the current local API exceeded the five-second
  source deadline. The actual UI rendered an unavailable alert and no empty-copy
  claim. Earlier successful live-paper flows remain dated evidence, not a claim
  that the external service answered this later probe.
- The streamed-loading fixture uses the same local origin and `nosniff`/no-store
  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the
  temporary review endpoint; it keeps the real progress assertions.
- Automated contrast/layout checks do not replace a screen-reader usability
  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.
- Hosted feature enablement, Redis-backed hosted paper journeys and the first
  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,
  hosted credentials, storage or production deployment settings were changed.

analysis_refs.heading: Remaining release gates
analysis_refs.text:
- Hosted shared Redis REST binding and explicit per-source budgets; flags remain
  off without them. Local Gutenberg search requires no database.
- Reviewed real children’s metadata and local app journeys are now complete.
  The three StoryWeaver books require a free source account, as accepted by the
  owner; no source account was created and post-login reading was not tested.
- Automated reviewed catalog refresh before 24-hour access evidence expiry;
  the candidate tool/daily draft-PR workflow are now implemented and tested
  locally; first scheduled execution follows default-branch merge. Stale evidence
  remains unknown. No global Gutenberg/OTL completeness or deletion claim.
- Finish board-state coverage, source-specific retraction/version fixtures,
  fresh protected preview and final hosted release checks. WebKit runs in CI;
  Firefox is not part of the existing CI browser matrix and has not been run here.

analysis_refs.text: | Hybrid | Independent catalog search plus specialist coverage | Two ingestion paths, provenance reconciliation | Recommended |

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Fit with the current repository
analysis_refs.text: Do not add global indexes to the geographic library directory. Preserve existing ISBN/work/catalog keys; introduce content keys independently. Adding papers to shelves needs an explicit later storage decision. The outbound-link MVP needs no shelf migration. Current Vercel requests must not depend on writable local disk or SQLite.

analysis_refs.heading: 6. Persistence, refresh and operations
analysis_refs.text: Use managed PostgreSQL for the bounded local catalogs, identifiers, relations, locations, source policies and harvest checkpoints. Coordinate with planned account persistence; this is not approval for migrations or a universal catalog. PostgreSQL full-text search can serve initial catalogs; add a specialized engine only when size, typo tolerance or multilingual needs justify it. Test Tamil/Indic and other non-Latin queries; English stemming is not multilingual search.

analysis_refs.heading: 6. Persistence, refresh and operations
analysis_refs.text: Import sequence: approved metadata fetch → size/schema/revision validation → normalized staging → count/deletion sanity checks → reconciliation → atomic index activation. Commit OAI pages before checkpointing. Use overlapping datestamp windows, idempotent upserts, tombstones and periodic reconciliation. Granularity/deletion support vary. Expired resumption tokens restart safely from durable windows. Failed/empty snapshots must never wipe the catalog.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text: Exit: every enabled provider has ingestion permission, refresh owner, stable link mapping and tested access policy. Partner-pending/catalog-only coverage stays explicitly scoped.

analysis_refs.heading: Result and evidence boundary
analysis_refs.text:
Status is **probed / recommended for owner review**, not production-qualified or
enabled. The full five-known-item/five-topic benchmark, repeated-session
reliability, accessibility/browser journeys and country-specific rights/access
checks remain later qualification tasks. Byte-range PDF/audio checks establish
anonymous retrieval of the sampled files; they do not certify every page or a
complete listening experience. No adapter, runtime manifest, source flag, catalog
import, deployment, database, scheduled task or source account was added.

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
No paid fallback is proposed. All tested search requests worked anonymously.
Respect current provider limits and use bounded requests, cancellation, backoff
and truthful unavailable states. No numeric unlimited allowance is inferred where
documentation does not publish one. Wikimedia calls should be serial with a
descriptive User-Agent and maxlag for research; Internet Archive also requests
identification of automated clients. LibriVox documents a maximum page size of
500 and pacing for bulk work. We requested only three catalog records at a time,
except GDL's fixed 20-record search page.

analysis_refs.heading: Alternatives investigated but withheld from the ten
analysis_refs.text: | NCERT | Official catalog is known from the discovery playbook | Catalog request returned HTTP 503 here. No current machine-search or metadata route was demonstrated in this batch. Revisit supported feeds/exports; this is not a claim of source-wide downtime. |

analysis_refs.heading: Alternatives investigated but withheld from the ten
analysis_refs.text: | Project Madurai | Official works catalog downloaded | A maintained and permitted metadata-search route still needs evidence. Public reading availability alone is insufficient. |

analysis_refs.heading: Alternatives investigated but withheld from the ten
analysis_refs.text: | OpenStax | CMS catalog, biology search and detail endpoints returned records | Current external-use support for the tested CMS route remains unestablished; measure existing OTL overlap and prefer documented OTL metadata where appropriate. |

analysis_refs.heading: Alternatives investigated but withheld from the ten
analysis_refs.text: | Lever Press via Thoth | API requests completed | Selected active-book query and small catalog probe returned no works. This does not prove the publisher has no free books; inspect another supported catalog route later. |

analysis_refs.heading: Coverage and the next decision
analysis_refs.text:
G01 covers children, books, scholarly books/textbooks and audio. This first batch
demonstrates each broad area but is weighted toward scholarly publishers; it is
not ten sources per category. Hindi, Tamil and India-related historical material
were sampled. No newly qualified India-operated catalog or current Indian school
curriculum collection is claimed. That remains an explicit discovery gap.

analysis_refs.heading: Books, children's reading and audiobooks: discovery recipes
analysis_refs.text:
The discovery chain is **directory/network → independently maintained catalog →
permitted retrieval route → matching item → evidenced free destination**. A
directory, an aggregator and the same underlying publisher are not three origins.
Reach 100 through additional useful catalogs, not additional mirrors, languages,
formats, narrators or books within a catalog.

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
```text
site:{publisher-domain} ("free stories" OR "digital library" OR "open licence")
"{language}" "children's books" ("Creative Commons" OR "open access")
"{publisher name}" (metadata OR API OR catalog OR download)
"हिन्दी बाल कहानियाँ" "मुक्त" / "தமிழ் சிறுவர் கதைகள்" "இலவசம்"
```

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
Repeat the native-language pattern with locally appropriate vocabulary; search
terms are discovery prompts, not evidence that results are lawful or free. Follow
actual book credits back to publishers and translators. Expand in batches of 25
origins across new country/language cells; use the measured pass rate to replenish
the pool toward 100 qualified origins. A national section is not automatically a
publisher and a translation of the same catalog does not add an origin.

analysis_refs.heading: C01. Children's books and early literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Prefer attributed coverage in an approved catalog,
an official export, or a supported publisher interface. An open-source website
codebase does not grant API access or metadata reuse. Free reader registration is
acceptable when disclosed; an advertised offer and verified post-login access are
separate observations. Recheck the existing StoryWeaver gate before expanding it.

analysis_refs.heading: C02. General books and ebooks
analysis_refs.text:
**Best starting points.** [Project Gutenberg's official catalog documentation](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/offline_catalogs.html)
identifies machine-readable catalogs, OPDS and affiliate/mirror links. Use the
catalog as a retrieval model; mirrors are duplicate hosting. National libraries,
state digital libraries, regional literary organizations and university special
collections supply additional independent origins. The [Library of Congress
JSON/YAML interface](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/) is a US starting
point for digitized collection records; its scope is not the entire library catalog.
DPLA's [developer documentation](https://pro.dp.la/developers/api-codex) is a
US aggregator lead requiring a fresh documentation/access check before selection.

analysis_refs.heading: C02. General books and ebooks
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Search `"{country/state}" "digital library" "literature"`,
`site:{institution-domain} ("digitized books" OR "ebooks" OR "rare books")`,
then `"{catalog name}" (OPDS OR MARC OR RDF OR API OR metadata)`. For each
national/state network, follow its digitization partners to catalog owners.
Expand the pool by geography, language and literature type; count independently
maintained catalogs only after recording attribution and a searchable subset.
Compare holdings with existing Gutenberg coverage before prioritizing a connector.

analysis_refs.heading: C02. General books and ebooks
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Import official reusable metadata into a bounded
local search artifact, use permitted OPDS search when available, or verify an
aggregator's origin attribution. Gutenberg's documentation currently mentions
OPDS2 testing and planned retirement of its XML OPDS feed in 2027; recheck before
choosing a long-term interface. Search-engine site results are not a substitute
for an in-app catalog. Record OCR/full-text availability separately from metadata
search; a digitized scan may be readable without searchable OCR.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**India route.** Investigate [NCERT's textbook catalog](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php),
state textbook bodies, university presses and e-PG Pathshala-linked institutions.
Start with official institution lists, then find their publication catalogs and
terms. An NCERT/state-board website with downloadable books is a candidate, not
evidence of an available external search API. Treat school medium, syllabus and
academic year as scope fields, not merely title keywords.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Enumerate publisher-origin candidates from approved metadata
exports by discipline, language and geography; inspect batches of 25 distinct
publishers. Search `"{university press}" "open access books"`,
`"{subject}" "open textbook" "{country}"`, and
`site:{education-body-domain} (textbook OR publication) (catalog OR download)`.
Follow open-education network members into their own catalogs and compare against
DOAB/OTL holdings. To approach 100, add qualified publisher catalogs across
disciplines, not 100 series from one press. Record the fraction actually covered
by the aggregator; a few OA titles never imply a wholly free publisher catalog.

analysis_refs.heading: C04. Textbooks and scholarly books/chapters
analysis_refs.text:
**First ten leads:** four Indian educational publishers/institutions, four new
publishers represented in DOAB/OTL, and two independently maintained catalogs from
underrepresented regions. Deep-review a publisher represented by an export and
an India school-text catalog to compare integration and refresh effort.

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**Search process.** Search `"{language}" "public domain audiobooks"`,
`"{institution}" ("talking books" OR audiobooks) (catalog OR API OR RSS)`,
and native-script equivalents for recorded stories/books. Follow a catalog's
producer credits to independently maintained origins. Expand by language/country
and producer type; distinguish library catalogs, volunteer recording projects and
publishers. A LibriVox narrator, recording version or mirror is not a new origin.
Expect a lower qualification rate and document scarcity if 100 independent,
freely accessible catalogs cannot be established.

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval to investigate.** Use native catalog APIs, approved aggregator
metadata, or complete reusable feeds compiled locally. A podcast feed containing
recent episodes may cover only a short window, not a book archive. Preserve
recording ID, work relation, narrator, language, abridgement, chapter order and
duration. Link the original player or permitted file; do not rehost audio.

analysis_refs.heading: C05. Audiobooks and recorded books
analysis_refs.text:
**First ten leads:** four India-language recording/catalog operators, four
independent international audio origins and two library/cultural audio catalogs.
If eligible candidates are scarce, record deferred leads explicitly; do not fill
the batch with paid trials, disability-entitled collections or podcast episodes.

analysis_refs.heading: Shared starting points
analysis_refs.text:
- **International:** [ILO sectors](https://www.ilo.org/topics-and-sectors/industries-and-sectors)
  links sector programs and guidance. Use its sector/country networks to find
  additional publishers. [FAO publications](https://www.fao.org/publications/en)
  links its knowledge repository; [WHO publications](https://www.who.int/publications)
  supplies health-related guidance; [IMO's Maritime Knowledge Centre](https://www.imo.org/en/knowledgecentre/pages/default.aspx)
  is a maritime discovery lead. Admission is per free item, not organization.
- **USA:** follow regulator publication catalogs, the [USDA land-grant institution
  directory](https://www.nifa.usda.gov/land-grant-colleges-and-universities-partner-website-directory)
  and [NIST MEP centers](https://www.nist.gov/mep/centers) into independently
  maintained extension/training catalogs. A center offering paid consulting can
  still publish free material; its whole service catalog is not free content.
- **India:** [NQR](https://www.nqr.gov.in/) exposes sectors, awarding bodies and
  job-role qualifications, and announces migration to [Kaushalverse](https://kaushalverse.ncvet.gov.in/homepage/repository).
  Check both during discovery and preserve original qualification IDs/version.
  [Bharat Skills](https://bharatskills.gov.in/) offers trade learning resources;
  [NSDC occupational standards and model curricula](https://nsdcindia.org/national-occupational-standards-and-model-curriculum)
  leads to sector councils and qualification packs. Their website search does
  not establish a reusable API or permission to reproduce metadata.

analysis_refs.heading: Shared starting points
analysis_refs.text:
In the matrix, **catalog probe** means investigate a documented API, permitted
metadata export or bounded reusable index. It does not mean scrape whichever
internal endpoint powers a website. Searches are discovery recipes to run against
official sites, then repeat for other countries, languages and institutions.

analysis_refs.heading: Industry-specific discovery matrix
analysis_refs.text: | **I01 Agriculture and horticulture** — crop planning, soil management, irrigation, extension work | FAO; USDA land-grant directory → each university extension publication catalog | [ICAR agricultural universities](https://www.icar.org.in/en/list-agricultural-universities) → state universities/KVKs; NQR Agriculture | `site:{extension-domain} "drip irrigation" (manual OR guide)`. Catalog probe by crop, region and language; retrieve the exact edition and actual guide. Expand through independent universities, not every extension office as a new origin. |

analysis_refs.heading: Industry-specific discovery matrix
analysis_refs.text: | **I08 Chemicals and pharmaceuticals** — process operations, quality assurance, manufacturing guidance | [FDA guidance catalog](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents); WHO; ILO chemicals/pharmaceuticals | NQR Chemicals & Petrochemicals/Life Sciences; [CDSCO](https://cdsco.gov.in/) guidance as a lead | `site:{regulator-domain} "good manufacturing" guidance`. Probe draft/final/superseded status, product class and jurisdiction. Retain issuing authority and revision rather than collapsing similarly titled guidelines. |

analysis_refs.heading: Industry-specific discovery matrix
analysis_refs.text:
The row links to roots such as CPWD, NHTSA, CDSCO, MNRE, MSHA, CPCB, DGCA and
RBI are institution leads requiring deeper catalog inspection. The generic
registry entries identify the correct sector/awarding-body trail, not a claim that
every qualification has a publicly reusable handbook.

analysis_refs.heading: Repeatable search and qualification process
analysis_refs.text:
1. **Authority route:** sector regulator → publications/guidelines → state/local
   counterparts → independently maintained catalogs. Check applicability and
   version. Twenty departments publishing through one catalog are not twenty
   automatically qualified origins.
2. **Training route:** qualification register → awarding body/sector council →
   public handbook/curriculum catalog → institution publishers. Qualification
   descriptions alone establish skills or curriculum, not full training content.
3. **Practice route:** extension/technical-center network → institutional resource
   collections → official manufacturer/project manuals where freely accessible.
   Publisher member lists are candidate generators; membership proves no API.

analysis_refs.heading: Repeatable search and qualification process
analysis_refs.text:
Try exact strings such as `"{role}" "participant handbook"`,
`site:{official-domain} "{task}" (manual OR guide OR curriculum)` and native-script
equivalents. Then search the selected provider for `API`, `metadata`, `export`,
`repository`, `license` and `reuse`. External search-engine matches help find
providers; they do not become app catalog records by themselves.

analysis_refs.heading: Repeatable search and qualification process
analysis_refs.text:
Use a documented live/aggregator interface where available, otherwise a permitted
metadata import searched locally. A small static registry and bounded catalog
artifacts fit the existing no-new-datastore approach. Shared transport/parsers can
serve several sources, but permissions and field mapping remain source-specific.
Record metadata reuse separately from the right to read a publicly downloadable
manual; public availability alone does not authorize bulk reproduction.

analysis_refs.heading: Documentation review limits
analysis_refs.text:
This review inspected primary web documentation/catalog pages, not production
API requests or a hundred sources per industry. O*NET explicitly documents an
API and downloadable data; reuse that as vocabulary evidence only until the
chosen integration is tested. The NQR migration notice was observed directly.
FDA/FAA/OSHA/NIST, ROSA P, FAO/WHO/IMO and Bharat Skills pages were readable.
India's ICAR, MSME, FSSAI, NHM and CERT-In discovery links also appeared in official
search results; catalog/permissions checks remain necessary.

analysis_refs.heading: C14 — Language learning and adult literacy
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Investigate attributed aggregator records and permitted
OAI/catalog imports. LINCS/Bharatavani website search alone does not establish a
reusable external API. Test an exact primer, a target-language topic, native
script, transliteration, an adult-versus-child distinction and the complete
lesson/audio destination. Preserve proficiency labels when supplied; do not infer
them from word count. Corpus access restrictions and missing machine interfaces
are likely reasons to defer candidates. Deep-review two distinct producers first.

analysis_refs.heading: C15 — Historical documents, manuscripts and archives
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Use [Archives Portal Europe's institution directory](https://www.archivesportaleurope.net/find-an-institution/)
to branch by country and holding institution. Its current page directs researchers
to institution search while directory work continues. In the US,
[NARA's Catalog API documentation](https://www.archives.gov/research/catalog/help/api)
describes keyword/search-result and individual-record JSON retrieval. Extend
discovery through state archives, university special collections and municipal
archive directories. In India, the National Archives'
[Abhilekh Patal description](https://nationalarchives.nic.in/en/online-portal-abhilekh-patal)
is the national starting point; follow state archives, regional record centers
and university manuscript collections separately.

analysis_refs.heading: C15 — Historical documents, manuscripts and archives
analysis_refs.text:
**Toward 100.** Start with four Indian holding institutions, two US federal/state
origins and four non-US international archives. Replenish from institutional
directories and regional archival networks. Record centers under one maintained
catalog are collections unless independent catalog stewardship is demonstrated.
Neither a directory's institution total nor a count of archival finding aids is
the enabled-source total.

analysis_refs.heading: C15 — Historical documents, manuscripts and archives
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer supported archival search or licensed EAD/OAI
exports with origin attribution. NARA documents a machine route; current key,
terms and limits still require review. Abhilekh Patal's external integration route
is unverified here. A finding aid may describe an undigitized box: require an
actual digitized object for usable online access. Test collection → series → item
hierarchy, reference code, date range, historical place aliases and a multipage
object. A IIIF manifest can describe/display a known object; separately prove
catalog discovery. Flag missing OCR rather than promising handwritten full-text
search. Deep-review one supported catalog and one Indian-origin candidate first.

analysis_refs.heading: C16 — Museums, art and cultural heritage
analysis_refs.text:
**Repeatable searches.** Run `"{country}" "museum" "open access collections"`,
`site:{museum-domain} (API OR IIIF OR "collection data" OR "metadata download")`
and `"{Indian state}" "museum" "digital collection"`. Follow departmental
collection links to confirm who maintains the catalog before assigning an origin.

analysis_refs.heading: C16 — Museums, art and cultural heritage
analysis_refs.text:
**Toward 100.** First ten: four Indian museums, two US institutions and four
international museums identified through aggregators. Expand by institution,
country and collection discipline: visual art, archaeology, textiles, craft,
natural history and technology. Different departments, exhibitions and objects
under one catalog do not become additional sources. Measure whether an added
institution contributes new languages or material rather than duplicate records.

analysis_refs.heading: C16 — Museums, art and cultural heritage
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer attributed aggregate search or official catalog
APIs/exports. Keep object metadata rights, image rights and physical-object
ownership separate. Verify an object identifier, creator/culture where supplied,
date uncertainty, place, institution and viewable media. Test a known object,
material/technique query, multilingual title and duplicate depiction. A tiny
thumbnail or metadata-only entry does not prove access to usable educational
media; declare the available representation. Require item-level permission and
attribution, including any restriction notices. Deep-review one aggregator-backed
origin and one direct-origin route before proposing a shared museum connector.

analysis_refs.heading: C17 — Newspapers, magazines and public-interest articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Toward 100.** First ten: two Indian historical collections, two Indian current
publishers, two US archival/news origins and four other-country origins. Expand
by language, city/state, publication period and publisher network. Several titles
owned by the same maintained publisher catalog remain one origin. A syndication
copy does not automatically constitute new reporting coverage.

analysis_refs.heading: C17 — Newspapers, magazines and public-interest articles
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Investigate supported archive APIs or permitted publisher
feeds/exports. [WordPress documents searchable post retrieval](https://developer.wordpress.org/rest-api/reference/posts/),
but a publisher's deployed endpoint and external-use terms still need validation.
RSS may contain only recent headlines; declare that window or find a supported
back-catalog route. Test issue/date/page identity separately from article identity,
OCR versus title matches, corrections, paywall/preview exclusions and original
publisher attribution. Test an older article beyond the first feed page before
claiming historical search. Deep-review one archive and one current publisher;
mixed paywalls and unclear reuse policies are expected qualification losses.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Where to start.** Begin with universities, public educational broadcasters and
institutional media producers, following their series/catalog links. In India,
[NPTEL's course catalog](https://nptel.ac.in/courses) provides instructor/course
and institutional discovery leads; investigate official educational broadcaster
and university series alongside it. For international and US material, inspect
university lecture catalogs and public-media learning collections. The
[Internet Archive developer portal](https://archive.org/developers/) documents
metadata tools for archive-hosted media; [Wikimedia Commons API guidance](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Commons:API)
supports another metadata route, with license and exclusion markers to review.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Repeatable searches.** Run `"{university/broadcaster}" "public lectures"`,
`"{subject}" "educational podcast" "RSS"`, and
`site:{official-domain} ("media catalog" OR API OR "video lectures" OR feed)`.
For India include Hindi/Tamil topic terms and the producer's official language
channel. A commercial streaming-platform listing is only a discovery clue.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Toward 100.** First ten: four Indian educational producers, two US producers
and four elsewhere. Expand by discipline, teaching language and institutional
network; count the producing catalog once across its video channel, podcast feed
and mirror. Series, playlists and episodes are not independent source origins.
Full documentaries with suitable access and reusable discovery may be scarcer
than lectures; publish that gap rather than filling it with trailers.

analysis_refs.heading: C20 — Educational podcasts, lectures and documentaries
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval and tests.** Prefer documented catalogs, attributed archive records
or permitted RSS/Atom imports. NPTEL's visible catalog does not establish an
external API in this review. Preserve episode/lecture ID, series/course relation,
producer, language, date, duration and canonical playback URL. Test a complete
recording, removed media, country restriction, premium-only episode and a caption
or transcript where available. Metadata search must not be described as searching
every spoken word. Hosting on an archive or public platform does not establish
lawful free access for every upload. Deep-review one feed-based producer and one
catalog-based producer before selecting a reusable media connector.

analysis_refs.heading: C10 — Courses, lecture notes and teaching materials
analysis_refs.text:
**Start with teaching institutions, not course-count leaderboards.** The
[Open Education Global member directory](https://www.oeglobal.org/about-us/members-list/)
is a repeatable route to international institutional leads, including community
colleges and regional open-education networks. Investigate each member's own
open course catalog, repository and public lecture-note collections. Membership
alone does not mean that it publishes eligible material. Use institutional
OpenCourseWare catalogs, including [MIT OCW](https://ocw.mit.edu/search/), as
examples of course organization; this review extracted only a shell from MIT's
search page, so it establishes no machine-search route.

analysis_refs.heading: C10 — Courses, lecture notes and teaching materials
analysis_refs.text:
For India, [SWAYAM's official overview](https://swayam.gov.in/about) identifies
national coordinators including NPTEL, UGC, CEC, NCERT, NIOS and IGNOU. Follow
coordinator → participating institution → official course/lesson catalog.
Record the producer institution and distribution platform separately. SWAYAM
describes free course learning and paid certification exams; the destination's
actual learning-access conditions still need review.

analysis_refs.heading: C10 — Courses, lecture notes and teaching materials
analysis_refs.text:
**Search recipe:** `site:{institution-domain} ("open courseware" OR "lecture
notes" OR "course materials") "{subject}"`, followed by semester/course-code
queries. Sample humanities and social sciences as well as engineering; expand
through country, language and discipline. University departments within one
shared catalog are not independently counted origins by default.

analysis_refs.heading: C11 — Encyclopedias, dictionaries and reference works
analysis_refs.text:
In India, [Bharatavani's dictionary collection](https://www.bharatavani.in/home/dictionaries)
is a lead to multilingual dictionaries, glossaries and their publishers. Its
catalog describes both searchable and PDF-based resources. Follow credited
language academies, universities and terminology bodies, and investigate local
reference resources in Hindi, Tamil and additional scripts. Elsewhere, use the
same language-academy/university approach rather than filling the register with
English-language general encyclopedias.

analysis_refs.heading: First research batch and route to 100 in each category
analysis_refs.text: | C09 | One Indian curriculum catalog and one independently maintained teacher-OER catalog |

analysis_refs.heading: First research batch and route to 100 in each category
analysis_refs.text: | C10 | One coordinator-linked Indian course origin and one international university's reusable catalog |

analysis_refs.heading: First research batch and route to 100 in each category
analysis_refs.text: | C11 | One supported entry-search wiki and one Indian dictionary/terminology catalog, explicitly testing search depth |

analysis_refs.heading: First research batch and route to 100 in each category
analysis_refs.text: | C13 | One Indian training/extension catalog and one US or other-country practical-publication catalog |

analysis_refs.heading: Research matrix
analysis_refs.text: | **P01 Government, research and development reports — C08** | [GovInfo Developer Hub](https://www.govinfo.gov/developers), agency publication catalogs, state research bureaus, municipal annual reports; follow publishing agencies from catalog records | Ministry/department publication sections reached through the [National Portal](https://www.india.gov.in/); RBI, NITI Aayog, research councils and state economic-survey series as leads | Topic/title/year/issuing body → report ID, edition, publication date and full report. A press release announcing a report is not the report. |

analysis_refs.heading: Find sources systematically, jurisdiction by jurisdiction
analysis_refs.text:
For India use Union → state/UT → district → subdistrict/tehsil → municipality or
village/panchayat. The [India district web directory](https://www.india.gov.in/directory/web-directory/districts)
and [Local Government Directory dataset](https://data.gov.in/catalog/local-government-directory-lgd)
are starting points. Follow official revenue, registration, planning, statistical
and geological offices from there. Record renamed/split districts and the vintage
of boundary codes; a village name alone is not a stable record identity.

analysis_refs.heading: Find sources systematically, jurisdiction by jurisdiction
analysis_refs.text:
```text
P01: site:{agency-domain} (publications OR reports) "{topic}" "{year}"
P02: site:{legislature-or-gazette-domain} "{act/rule title}" "{jurisdiction}"
P03: site:{city-domain} (minutes OR resolutions OR budget OR awards) "{year}"
P04: "{county/state}" (recorder OR assessor OR land records) (API OR open data)
P05: site:{planning-domain} (permits OR zoning OR master plan) (catalog OR GIS)
P06: "{state}" "geological survey" (map catalog OR GIS OR publications)
P07: site:{mapping-agency-domain} "{place/sheet}" (topographic OR land cover)
P08: site:{statistics-domain} "{indicator}" "{district/county}" (table OR API)
P09: site:{agency-domain} "{water/transport/environment theme}" (data OR services)
```

analysis_refs.heading: From a directory entry to something the app can query
analysis_refs.text:
1. **Official document/dataset catalog API.** [GovInfo documents an API search
   service](https://www.govinfo.gov/features/search-service-overview) for content
   and metadata. The current [Data.gov Catalog API](https://resources.data.gov/catalog-api/)
   searches dataset metadata and identifies publisher organizations; it explicitly
   replaces the previous CKAN API. Use the current interface and key policy,
   not an old tutorial. An indexed dataset still needs a valid resource link.
2. **Approved exports and local metadata search.** Small DCAT/CSV/JSON/XML catalogs
   can become bounded, reviewed search artifacts without a hosted database. Prefer
   metadata and canonical outbound links; do not copy whole national parcel or
   imagery stores to make a prototype searchable.
3. **Native record or feature queries.** A source can qualify for property or
   spatial lookup through real address/parcel/document-ID/area queries even when
   it lacks general keyword search. This must return record metadata and a usable
   destination; an identifier-shaped redirect to an external search page is not
   retrieval. Record this as a separate capability from topic discovery.
4. **Geo services with explicit discovery.** [OGC WFS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wfs/),
   [OGC API Features](https://www.ogc.org/standards/ogcapi-features/) and documented
   [ArcGIS layer queries](https://developers.arcgis.com/rest/services-reference/enterprise/query-feature-service-layer/)
   are patterns to inspect for spatial/attribute filtering. Confirm the deployed
   service's capabilities, limits, IDs and terms; the platform brand is not proof.
   [WMS](https://www.ogc.org/standards/wms/)/WMTS primarily deliver rendered maps
   or tiles. A searchable layer catalog can support map discovery, but does not
   establish searchable parcel attributes or downloadable source features.

analysis_refs.heading: From a directory entry to something the app can query
analysis_refs.text:
Track three separate capabilities: **find a dataset/map/document**, **query
records within it**, and **read/view/download the result**. A catalog hit for
property data cannot answer “which record covers this parcel?” unless the second
capability is present. Conversely a spatial result can be useful without hosting
a map renderer: a precise official map/document link is a valid initial action.

analysis_refs.heading: First batch and acceptance tests
analysis_refs.text:
Allocate **six US and six India origins within the overall 60-origin deep-review
cap**, deduplicating any shared candidates. This is not an additional 12 reviews.
For each country select one reports/law route, one civic-budget route, one
property route, one permits/planning route, one geological/topographic route and
one statistics/environment route. Within a broad national catalog, inspect the
origin-specific attribution; include state/local cases rather than selecting
only national aggregators. NYC and Tamil Nadu are initial local case studies.

analysis_refs.heading: C03 — Published research articles
analysis_refs.text:
Resolve organization names to stable identities before counting. The first
research batch is ten independent origins: four Indian, four broadly accessible
international and two additional regional-language origins. Deep-review one
publisher and one repository with the greatest apparent coverage gap. Expand in
25-origin batches across countries, disciplines and organization types toward
100 qualified origins; journal titles from one catalog do not become 100 origins.

analysis_refs.heading: C06 — Theses and dissertations
analysis_refs.text:
**Start from degree-granting institutions and national thesis networks.**
[NDLTD's FAQ](https://ndltd.org/thesis-resources/faqs/) describes a union catalog
made available to service providers and directs users to its current Find ETDs
resources; its navigation currently points Global ETD Search to OATD. Treat this
as a directory/coverage route, not evidence of a turnkey NDLTD keyword API.
Cross-reference university origins through OpenDOAR.

analysis_refs.heading: C06 — Theses and dissertations
analysis_refs.text: | USA | Inspect official university library ETD policies and institutional repositories. Check whether the institution supplies open deposits or only points to a commercial dissertation service. University departments are not extra origins when their theses share one maintained catalog. |

analysis_refs.heading: C06 — Theses and dissertations
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval strategy.** Verify attributed aggregator coverage with known thesis
titles first. Otherwise inspect the repository's advertised OAI-PMH/export or
documented API. OAI-PMH requires an import and local title/topic search; it is not
a live keyword endpoint. Discover actual supported routes and versions instead
of guessing DSpace paths. Start with a bounded, disclosed metadata subset using
the existing catalog approach; no new hosted database is prerequisite.

analysis_refs.heading: C07 — Preprints and working papers
analysis_refs.text:
For the first ten origins, investigate four Indian institution collections, three
international disciplinary servers and three institutional series from other
regions, including the USA. Deep-review one server and one working-paper archive.
To approach 100, replenish both paths in batches of 25 and deduplicate operators.
There may not be 100 suitable independent preprint servers; institutional
working-paper catalogs supply a distinct, valid part of this category. One
university's many series still count as one catalog origin under the main rules.

analysis_refs.heading: Source catalog and connection options
analysis_refs.text: # Source catalog and connection options

analysis_refs.heading: 1. General ebooks and public-domain literature
analysis_refs.text: | **Project Gutenberg — host** | Import official CSV/RDF catalog into local search; PG ID as identity. Official OPDS supports discovery. [Catalog formats](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/offline_catalogs.html), [automation policy](https://www.gutenberg.org/policy/robot_access.html) | `https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/{id}`; metadata supplies HTML/EPUB/text format URLs. Public-domain status is generally US-specific; preserve per-record rights. | No key. Use approved catalog distribution, not website search scraping. Docs mentioned OPDS2 testing and planned XML feed retirement in 2027. RDF sample worked. **Medium / P0**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 1. General ebooks and public-domain literature
analysis_refs.text: | **Standard Ebooks — host** | OPDS 1/2 `/feeds/opds`; public new-release RSS/Atom. [Feed rules](https://standardebooks.org/feeds) | Canonical ebook page and formats. Publisher-produced content is CC0; third-party material and public-domain jurisdiction need separate care. | Full feeds are a Patrons Circle/producer/sponsor benefit. Personal membership is not automatic permission to redistribute a catalog through an app. Confirm integration terms; new-release feed alone is incomplete. **Medium/high / P2**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Textbooks, education and children's reading
analysis_refs.text: | **Open Textbook Library — textbook index** | [Discovery docs](https://open.umn.edu/opentextbooks/discovery): MARC, CSV, textbook/subject `.json`, RSS/Atom, deleted lists. Prefer import/local search. | Catalog CC0; books have individual licenses/hosts. Preserve edition/subject/language/license. Docs reviewed, JSON search semantics not probed. | No credential specified for public resources. **Medium / P0 education**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Textbooks, education and children's reading
analysis_refs.text: | **OpenStax — textbook host** | [Subjects](https://openstax.org/subjects); curated book records or Open Textbook Library coverage, then request supported machine catalog. | Free web/PDF vs paid print/products; inspect individual licenses. [Licensing page](https://openstax.org/license) rendered only app shell. | No public search API verified; internal website requests are not a supported contract. **Low curated, high full connector / P1**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Textbooks, education and children's reading
analysis_refs.text: | **NCERT / ePathshala — school books** | [NCERT catalog](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php); curate official pages by class/subject/language/edition or obtain feed. | Free reading is not open redistribution. Preserve academic year/edition and language. | NCERT got 503; machine API/feed unverified. **Medium/high / P2**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Textbooks, education and children's reading
analysis_refs.text: | **Book Dash — children's host** | [Current books catalog](https://bookdash.org/books/); curate or request export. | Picture books/translations/source materials; verify each license/credits and screen reader vs print-ready download. | The public WordPress book API and language taxonomy were verified on 2026-11-01; a pinned 30-English-edition subset is implemented with exact creator roles and public-gallery evidence. See [current source operations](ADDITIONAL_SOURCES.md). **Implemented bounded subset**. |

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Textbooks, education and children's reading
analysis_refs.text: A reviewed 50–100-book children's catalog is a useful explicit pilot scope, not a claim of comprehensive repository search. Do not infer age suitability from the word children in a subject string.

analysis_refs.heading: 6. Cultural collections, historical science and audio
analysis_refs.text: | **Library of Congress — host/index** | JSON/YAML `?fo=json`, search/collections/item resources. [API](https://www.loc.gov/apis/json-and-yaml/) | No key. Readable resources subset of catalog; per-item rights/access advisory. Books response worked, digitized/full-text classification not tested. | **Low/medium / P1**. |

analysis_refs.heading: Free books and research discovery
analysis_refs.text:
- [Source catalog](source-catalog.md): categories, repositories, connection methods, credentials, constraints, and priorities.
- [Architecture and delivery plan](architecture.md): contracts, query flow, storage, repository integration, and rollout gates.
- [Evidence](evidence.json): historical request URLs, observed outcomes, selected findings, and verification limits.

analysis_refs.heading: Recommendation
analysis_refs.text: Start with **Free books** and **Research papers**. Add **Textbooks & learning** through the Open Textbook Library catalog, then a curated **Children's books** collection. Treat language, subject, reading level, format, and access conditions as separate filters rather than mutually exclusive categories.

analysis_refs.heading: Recommendation
analysis_refs.text: | Open Textbook Library | Official CSV/JSON metadata; local search | Documented CC0 catalog for educational material |

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text:
- An Open Library work returned `ebook_access: public` alongside many Internet Archive identifiers. That does not identify which edition is freely readable.
- A HAL hit had a record URL and DOI but no `fileMain_s`: a repository hit is not necessarily full text.
- Zenodo returned a dataset; item-type filtering is essential.
- DOAJ supplied an older HTTP publisher URL; metadata alone does not prove the destination still works.
- Semantic Scholar returned **429**, and Gutendex timed out. Those checks do not establish general service availability.
- Some documentation URLs moved; corrected DOAB/OAPEN URLs appear in the catalog. Some sites returned only a JavaScript shell. NCERT/ERIC/OER Commons could not be fully inspected.

analysis_refs.heading: Credentials and implementation inputs
analysis_refs.text:
1. Verify **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** in the backend. The replacement environment reports the variable configured; no authenticated OpenAlex request was made during this repository transfer. At the research date the free account included $1/day of API usage, roughly 1,000 ordinary search requests before caching. Disable paid overages unless deliberately budgeted.
2. Choose a real **application contact email** for request identification and, if enabled, Unpaywall's required `email` parameter. No email was invented, registered, or sent during this work.
3. Optional later: Semantic Scholar, BHL and Europeana keys; CORE upgrade/eligibility confirmation. Standard Ebooks feed access and children's/OER catalog feeds need provider-specific arrangements.
